comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
The pattern seems fairly consistent:
- Caddy itself understands `fd/*` socket-activation addresses
- the ACME challenge listener path does not
- `fd/4` is ending up in a place where it is treated like a normal host string which is why we get errors like `lookup fd/4: no such host`

There are also now enough confirmations that the earlier workaround does not seem reliably sufficient in all setups.

So I think the remaining question is really which fix direction is wanted:
1. reject/ignore `fd/*` when adapting bind information into the ACME challenge listener path, with a clearer error
2. port fd/socket-activation support through to CertMagic’s embedded challenge listener path so this works end-to-end

Given Francis’s earlier comment, my read is that (2) is probably the correct long-term fix but the issue does still look open and real either way.

@participant1, thoughts?

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
I just encountered this issue after seeing that my certificates weren't renewed. Issue still exists and certmagic is not bumped to the latest version which is v0.25.4.

FWIW, if you have a custom Caddy image built with xcaddy, you can simply override the certmagic module version to use the latest one, like so:

```Dockerfile
FROM caddy:2.11-builder AS builder

RUN xcaddy build \
    --with github.com/caddyserver/certmagic@v0.25.4

FROM caddy:2.11-alpine
COPY --from=builder /usr/bin/caddy /usr/bin/caddy
```
